utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, the Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. In order to continue the examination of the witness, we turn to closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. The statement I'll read out addresses the Prosecution. The reason that it addresses the Prosecution is that the Prosecution expressed an intention to make -- to file a response to a certain matter. That's the one and only reason why it's not addressed to all parties. It is the Chamber's invitation to the Prosecution to respond to a submission recently made by the Republic of Croatia. In a submission dated the 2nd of June, 2009, the Republic of Croatia requested the Chamber to deliver a decision in relation to the Prosecution's application for an order pursuant to Rule 54 bis from the 13th of June, 2008. In an informal communication to the Chamber on the 8th of June, the Prosecution indicated that it wished to respond to this submission and to do so no later than the 18th of June, 2009. The Chamber hereby invites the Prosecution to respond to the submission by Croatia no later than the 18th of June, 2009. And in its response, the Chamber would like the Prosecution not only to address the arguments in the submissions, but also to deal with the general Rule 54 bis matter. In a filing of the 19th of January, 2009, the Prosecution already addressed this matter, but since then Croatia has submitted further documentation and reports pursuant to the Chamber's order of the 16th of September, 2008. The Chamber therefore provides the Prosecution with this further opportunity to be heard before the Chamber will decide on the matter. And this concludes the Chamber's statement. There would be a few procedural -- other procedural matters we could deal with, rather than to schedule a hearing for tomorrow or Friday, because the Chamber understands that there are no witnesses available for Thursday or Friday, but please correct me if I'm wrong, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: We just received that confirmation from VWS, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's about the passport of a witness. I would have for approximately 20 minutes of time, for procedural matters, mainly giving short decisions, receiving answers. I think if we organise that well, we could avoid having a hearing tomorrow or Friday, because everyone would have to come just for 20 minutes, which seems not to be a very effective use of especially your time. I'll therefore invite the -- I will therefore invite the Chamber staff to identify the issues in one-liners, so that once we have an opportunity we could go through them, not in 20 minutes, but most likely in 3 or 4 minutes, you knowing exactly what is at stake. It would, for example, read, Decision on admission, Exhibit so-and-so. Then you would know that we come with a decision, Response requested on issue so-and-so. Then we could stream-line and expedite those matters, which would avoid that we have to rely on the highly-appreciated cooperation of our interpreters, transcriber, and technical staff for going beyond the time-limits. We adjourn, and we'll resume on Monday, the 15th of June, 9.00, Courtroom III.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 15th day of June, 2009, at 9.00 a.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
